answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to complete a unique, non-parallelizable sequential proof of work before it earns weight: one long computation thread that cannot be split across machines, so an attacker wanting a hundred fake agents must pay a hundred times the wall-clock time and energy. Like a knoll that only reveals its view after the climb, reputation accrues only after this climb is finished, and the cost creates a ripple effect: cheap sock-puppets become uneconomical, while a single honest agent's one-time cost stays trivial.
